module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
public import Mathlib.Data.ENat.Lattice
public import Mathlib.Order.CompletePartialOrder

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph
variable {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}

open Finset List

@[inherit_doc] scoped notation "α(" G ")" => indepNum G

@[simp] lemma indepNum_of_isEmpty [IsEmpty V] : α(G) = 0 := by
  simp [indepNum, isNIndepSet_iff, Subsingleton.elim _ ∅]

@[simp] lemma indepNum_pos [Finite V] [Nonempty V] : 0 < α(G) := by
  cases nonempty_fintype V
  obtain ⟨v⟩ := ‹Nonempty V›
  rw [← Nat.add_one_le_iff]
  exact le_csSup ⟨Nat.card V, by simp [mem_upperBounds, isNIndepSet_iff, Finset.card_le_univ]⟩
    ⟨{v}, by simp [isNIndepSet_iff]⟩

/-- Infinite graphs: definitions for clique number so that the clique number of a graph
with unbounded clique size is `∞` rather than 0.
-/
noncomputable
def ecliqueNum {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ∞ := ⨆ (s : Finset V) (_ : G.IsClique s), #s

/-- The set of sizes of the cliques (maximal complete subgraphs) of `G`. -/
def cliqueSizes {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Set ℕ :=
  { k | ∃ S : Finset V, Maximal (fun T : Finset V => G.IsClique (T : Set V)) S ∧ S.card = k }

open scoped Classical in
/-- The triangles of `G` containing the edge `uv`, that is, the `3`-cliques of `G` whose vertex
set contains both endpoints of `uv`. -/
noncomputable def trianglesContaining {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (G : SimpleGraph α)
    (uv : Sym2 α) : Finset (Finset α) :=
  (G.cliqueFinset 3).filter (fun t ↦ uv.toFinset ⊆ t)


end SimpleGraph

status_issues.recorded: @[category research open], with answer(sorry), in FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/80.lean.
status_issues.source_status: The polynomial lower-bound subquestion was disproved by Fox and Loh, Combinatorica 32 (2012), 619–628. They obtain f_c(n) ≤ n^{O(1/log log n)} for every fixed 0 < c < 1/4, ruling out every positive power lower bound. The broader estimation problem and logarithmic lower-bound question remain open.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/80 explicitly says that Fox and Loh's bound is 'disproving the first conjecture of Erdős'. The abstract at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00493-012-2844-3 states the same polynomial question and says, 'This gives a negative answer to the question of Erdős.' Any fixed c in (0,1/4), such as 1/8, lies within the Lean statement's permitted range.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change Erdos80.erdos_80 to category research solved with answer(False), and cite Fox–Loh. Leave Erdos80.erdos_80.variants.log tagged research open.

reformulations.difference: Takes an ℕ∞-valued supremum over finite cliques rather than selecting a largest clique.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The scratch file proves ecliqueNum G ≤ n iff every finite clique has at most n vertices, and ecliqueNum G = ⊤ iff finite clique sizes are unbounded. It also proves ecliqueNum G = (G.cliqueNum : ℕ∞) for finite vertex types. Thus this is precisely the documented extended convention, including bounded-clique infinite graphs, not an erroneous supremum or a duplicate of the ℕ-valued Mathlib definition.

reformulations.difference: Tests maximality against finite vertex sets, whereas the usual definition permits arbitrary complete supersets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite clique S, any proper complete superset contains a vertex v outside S, and S ∪ {v} is already a proper finite complete extension. Conversely, a finite extension is a set extension. The scratch file proves this maximality equivalence without assuming the whole graph finite. Consequently the definition records exactly the finite maximal-clique sizes; its problem uses have finite vertex types. The maximal-clique terminology agrees explicitly with Erdős 775 and Gao's introduction.

reformulations.difference: Uses extended invariants on arbitrary graphs and the inequality 2 * χ ≤ ω + Δ + 2 instead of the usual ceiling bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For natural-number invariants, χ ≤ ceil((ω + Δ + 1)/2) is equivalent to 2χ ≤ ω + Δ + 2; this arithmetic equivalence was proved in the scratch file. The arbitrary-graph statement is equivalent to the finite-graph conjecture: infinite extended maximum degree makes the right side ⊤, while finite maximum degree also bounds clique sizes. Applying the finite conjecture to all finite induced subgraphs and then the de Bruijn–Erdős coloring compactness theorem gives the same bound for the whole graph. The full compactness-based equivalence was not proved in Lean.

reformulations.difference: Requires maximum degree exactly 6 and cliqueNum exactly 2, while the cited MathOverflow question concerns triangle-free graphs of maximum degree at most 6.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Adjoining a disjoint copy of the star K₁,₆ to any triangle-free graph of maximum degree at most 6 forces maximum degree 6 and clique number 2. A 5-coloring of the enlarged graph restricts to the original graph. The converse is immediate. Under the degree bound, finite clique sizes are bounded, so Mathlib's ordinary cliqueNum has no unbounded-supremum default issue. Coloring compactness also justifies allowing infinite vertex sets.

review.notes:
All six declarations in the reviewed file were checked, including the notation and both proved lemmas. No mathematical defect or duplicate Mathlib declaration was found. Problem-level uses of α have finite vertex types, and every triangle-counting caller restricts the unordered pair to edgeFinset. Diagonal pairs select triangles through one vertex, as the explicit endpoint-containment criterion specifies, but never occur in those callers.

/workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors, warnings, or sorryAx dependencies. It contains characterization proofs and tests covering empty and singleton graphs, complete and edgeless infinite graphs, maximal-clique sizes {1,3} for a triangle plus an isolated vertex, and triangle counts on K₄. The reviewed file remains unchanged. Erdős pages and the Fox–Loh abstract were retrieved through r.jina.ai after direct access challenges; WOWII was checked using archived statements and definitions because the live site timed out.
